Issued at 145 PM CDT Sun Oct 11 2026

This Afternoon - Monday Afternoon: Well Above Normal to Near Record 
Temperatures

Well above normal to near-record temperatures are expected to 
linger into Monday as upper level ridging and rising heights 
build into the region while southerly low level winds continue 
to usher warm air into the region. Mostly clear skies should 
allow for efficient mixing to around 850hPa where temperatures 
sit between 17-20C owing to this warm air advection, resulting 
in surface temperatures climbing into the 80s this afternoon and
Monday afternoon. High level cloud cover increases overnight 
into Monday morning which could hinder diurnal heating and high
temperatures a bit on Monday depending how long they linger 
across the region, but overall expectations are for skies to be 
mostly clear through much of the day. 

Monday Afternoon - Friday: Periodic Rain Chances, Trending Cooler

700hPa troughing moves into the area along with a surface low 
and associated frontal zones on Monday, with the warm front 
lifting northward through the region during the afternoon hours.
Showers and perhaps some rumbles of thunder given a few hundred
J/kg of elevated instability are expected along this boundary 
through the afternoon and into the evening, mainly north of I-94
where deeper moisture is expected. Current probabilities across
our area sit around 20-40% per the 11.12z HREF/REFS, higher 
across northern Wisconsin where stronger forcing along the front
and deeper moisture is expected. Given some dry air in the low 
levels, amounts will also be fairly low, generally 0.1-0.2" per 
the 11.13z NBM, but some higher amounts could be realized where 
the atmosphere is able to make use of the instability. The 
surface cold front then moves through the region Monday night 
into Tuesday before stalling across southern Iowa into northern 
Illinois, allowing for cooler temperatures to filter into the 
Upper Mississippi River Valley through the remainder of the 
week.

Another shot at some rainfall comes Tuesday evening into the 
overnight hours as another bout of shortwave energy moves over 
the stationary boundary that develops across Iowa into Illinois.
While the bulk of precipitation is expected to remain south of 
the area, more confined to the synoptic forcings as depicted by 
the various ensemble suites, those along and south of Highway 18
could see some rainfall during this period (20-50%).

Greater potential for showers comes Thursday into Friday 
morning as an upper level low and associated surface mid- 
latitude cyclone move into the Midwest. Higher confidence 
exists regarding rainfall potential during this period as noted
by the 11.13z NBM which has a 50-70% probability for measurable
rainfall along with some potential for amounts of 1/2" or more,
a 20-40% chance.

Drier conditions begin to develop Friday, but could see some 
scattered showers develop during the afternoon in the cold air 
advection regime on the backside of Thursday's low. That said, 
current probabilities of this are quite low, generally around 
10-15%.

Next Weekend: Cool, Mostly Dry

Fairly strong high pressure looks to sink into the central 
United States next weekend as the aforementioned low moves 
eastward and longwave ridging builds in from the west, resulting
in little potential for precipitation. A much cooler airmass is
also expected to accompany these synoptic features resulting in
near to slightly below normal temperatures. Exact temperature 
values are uncertain as quite a bit of temperature spread exists
within the various ensemble suites, upwards of 10-15 degrees. 
However, the overall trend is towards cooler temperatures with 
mean high temperatures in the 11.13z NBM in the mid 50s to low 
60s, around 5 degrees below normal. Overnight lows Friday into 
Saturday may also fall to around or below freezing, coldest 
across central into north-central Wisconsin.
